PyTorch’s [GRU equations](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/main/generated/torch.nn.GRU.html) explain a likely padding failure: zero input can still update hidden state through biases and recurrent dynamics; a zero padding embedding alone does not guarantee invariance. Recommended localization: compare identical item histories with different amounts of leading padding, inspecting valid-position features before candidate scores. Skip recurrent updates on padding, or compact valid tokens into right-padded sequences before [packing](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/main/generated/torch.nn.utils.rnn.pack_padded_sequence.html), then restore alignment. For original left-padded histories, read the final nonpadding position, never `count-1`. Compare each history alone, in permuted batches, and after unrelated inference calls to distinguish batch coupling from persistent hidden-state leakage; GRU defaults to zero initial state when none is supplied.

Use evaluation mode and fixed candidates throughout. Compare the live model with a freshly reconstructed checkpoint and the generated predictor, including item mappings, architecture settings, features and scores; PyTorch recommends saving `state_dict` and calling `eval()` for inference ([serialization guide](https://docs.pytorch.org/tutorials/beginner/saving_loading_models)). These are proposed diagnostic relations, not measured findings. Preserve `log2feats`, `item_emb`, and `predict_score` throughout.

Calibrate absolute/relative error against repeated identical runs, then characterize batch-shape changes separately: PyTorch warns that batched and sliced computations need not be bitwise identical ([numerical accuracy](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/main/notes/numerical_accuracy.html)). Report nonfinite values, maximum errors and top-10 changes rather than simply widening tolerance. Following [DeepMutation’s](https://lilicoding.github.io/papers/ma2018deepmutation.pdf) sensitivity-testing principle, inject isolated diagnostic-only faults: unmasked padding updates, `count-1` readout, cached hidden state, and omitted checkpoint parameters. Require targeted probes to detect them; record undetected mutants without claiming the suite proves correctness.
